Re(AI)magining ™ the Enterprise Where AI Ambition Meets Engineering Execution Every generation of technology arrives with a promise. The promise of AI is the most consequential in decades, and this time, the potential is real. AI can reshape how organisations build software, serve customers, manage risk, accelerate discovery and make decisions. The investments are justified. The urgency is warranted. What is also real is this: many organisations are struggling to translate that promise into measurable impact. It is not because they lack access to models, platforms or ambition. The distance between AI strategy and operational reality, between boardroom commitment and production deployment is wider, more structurally complex and harder to close than many anticipated. Pilots that proved the concept have stalled before production. Data that seemed ready has turned out to be fragmented, inconsistent or ungoverned.

Agents that performed well in demonstrations have struggled in the messy, regulated and interconnected reality of large organisations. The gap is real and it is costing organisations time, capital and competitive ground. More fundamentally, AI is reshaping how organisations create value, compete and grow. The next competitive advantage will come from the ability to integrate intelligence into the operating core of the organisation. The organisations that succeed will not simply adopt AI. They will redesign how work gets done around it. This is the moment Persistent was built for. We chose this year's theme, Re(AI)magining ™ the Enterprise: Where AI Ambition Meets Engineering Execution, not to describe an aspiration, but to define where we create value. Persistent sits at the point where AI strategy becomes operational reality and where lasting advantage is created. That standing is earned, not claimed.

Persistent's heritage in software and product engineering places us at the intersection of AI, data and modernisation. For more than three decades, we have helped clients engineer complex technology systems that are resilient, scalable and business-critical. Those strengths are becoming increasingly relevant as organisations move from experimentation towards widespread adoption. They are reflected in our AI platforms, SASVA ™ , iAURA and GenAI Hub, and in the 3C Framework of Core, Context and Coordination. Together, they help organisations establish a strong technology foundation, apply intelligence with business context and embed AI into the workflows where decisions and outcomes are created. Importantly, these are not frameworks designed for presentation slides. They are disciplines built through real-world deployment, refined within Persistent as Customer Zero and applied across increasingly complex client environments.

That experience continues to shape how we help clients move from fragmented AI investments to trusted outcomes. The organisations we serve are at an inflection point. AI ambition is funded. The question now is execution. The next phase belongs to organisations capable of turning pilots into platforms, data into insight and governance into a foundation for growth. The winners will be those that can embed intelligence into the systems, workflows and decisions that drive business performance. This is where Persistent stands apart. We bring the engineering depth, data foundation, platform IP, governance discipline and delivery model required to help clients move from investment to measurable, trusted outcomes. FY26 showed what becomes possible when AI ambition meets engineering execution. This report is the story of that progress and the foundation for what comes next. 7 6 Persistent Systems Limited Annual Report 2026 7 6

Message from the Chairman Dr. Anand Deshpande Founder, Chairman and Managing Director It is a privilege to share Persistent Systems’ 36 th Annual Report. Each year provides an opportunity to pause in gratitude, reflect on how far we have come, and consider the changing world around us. Above all, it is an opportunity to acknowledge the trust that has made this journey possible. When we started Persistent in 1990, we had very limited resources. What we did have was curiosity, determination and a willingness to learn. We believed that if we remained useful to our customers and continued to create value for them, the business would grow. More than three decades later, those fundamentals remain unchanged. Trust of this kind is never built in boardrooms alone. It is earned every day through the actions of our people. It is built project by project, commitment by commitment, often quietly and away from public view.

Behind every customer relationship are teams that work diligently to solve problems, meet commitments and go the extra mile when needed. Their dedication, professionalism and care have helped Persistent earn the confidence of customers around the world, and I remain deeply grateful for their contribution. This year, much of the world’s attention turned decisively towards Artificial Intelligence. Few technologies in recent memory have generated such widespread interest, debate and investment. While every generation believes it is witnessing extraordinary change, there are moments when technology genuinely alters the trajectory of industries and societies. Like the Internet and mobile computing before it, I believe AI represents one such moment. Over the last several years, enterprises have been exploring how AI can improve productivity, automate tasks and create new possibilities. Much of the recent attention has focused on agents and automation.

These developments are important and are already creating value. However, I believe they represent only the beginning of a much larger transformation. Over the years, organisations have used software to streamline processes, improve efficiency and create consistency. AI introduces a new possibility: systems that can assist in interpretation, judgement and decision- making. We are entering a period in which intelligence itself is becoming a technology platform. The transition from automation to intelligence is now underway, and its implications extend far beyond technology. It will influence how organisations operate, innovate and compete. While much of the current discussion focuses on foundation models and their rapidly advancing capabilities, I believe the long- term value of AI will be determined not by the models themselves, but by how effectively organisations combine intelligence with their own data, knowledge and experience.

Over time, powerful models will become increasingly accessible. The more important differentiator will be context: an organisation’s enterprise data, customer relationships, business processes, operating history and accumulated expertise. Enterprises that successfully combine AI with this context will create advantages that are difficult to replicate. At the same time, organisations are being required to confront important questions around privacy, security, governance and data sovereignty. These considerations cannot be treated as afterthoughts. The future will require enterprises to balance innovation with trust, Dear Fellow Shareowners, As new technologies emerge, the most important differentiator will not simply be access to tools, but the ability to use them to solve real business problems. Technology will change many things, but judgement, creativity and integrity will still matter deeply. Persistent Systems Limited Annual Report 2026 9 8

As enterprises move from automation towards intelligence, these foundations become even more important. We believe that enterprise intelligence will ultimately depend on three elements: the platforms on which intelligence runs, the context that allows intelligence to understand the business and the coordination required to translate intelligence into action. This perspective shapes how we think about the future and how we help customers navigate it. While technologies will continue to evolve rapidly, our focus remains constant: helping customers create lasting value through the thoughtful application of technology. I am encouraged by how our people are responding to this moment. New technologies will continue to emerge, but the most important differentiators will remain the ability to learn, adapt and solve meaningful problems. Technology changes rapidly, while qualities such as judgement, creativity, integrity and perseverance endure.

These qualities have always been central to Persistent’s culture and will become even more important in the years ahead. Institutions become stronger when learning becomes part of their culture. As the pace of technological change accelerates, we must continue to create opportunities for our people to develop new skills, challenge assumptions and grow professionally. Persistent University and our broader investments in workforce capability remain important pillars of our long-term strategy. The future will belong to organisations that learn continuously, and we remain committed to building one. Our growth continued with consistency in FY26, marking our 24 th consecutive quarter of growth. This achievement reflects the trust of our customers, the strength of our strategy and the commitment of our people. I thank every employee for the professionalism, resilience and care they bring to their work each day.

I would also like to acknowledge the support of their families, whose encouragement and understanding make these achievements possible in countless ways. I remain deeply grateful to our customers for the trust they place in Persistent. Many of these relationships have evolved over years, and in some cases decades. Technology cycles change quickly. Relationships built on trust, performance and shared success endure. Those relationships continue to shape the company we are becoming and remain among our greatest strengths. Growth also brings broader responsibilities. Our commitments extend beyond business performance to sustainability, governance, innovation and community impact. Recognition through the Dow Jones Sustainability Indices and other ESG benchmarks is encouraging. More importantly, it reflects our effort to build a business that is responsible, resilient and sustainable over the long term.

We remain committed to creating value not only for shareowners, but also for customers, employees and the communities in which we operate. With warm regards, Dr. Anand Deshpande Founder, Chairman and Managing Director 10 11 Persistent Systems Limited Annual Report 2026

Re(AI)magining ™ the Enterprise Operationalising Intelligence at Scale Message from the CEO Sandeep Kalra Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer FY26 marked a defining year in the evolution of enterprise AI. Across industries, the conversation shifted decisively from experimentation to execution. Organisations are no longer asking what AI can do; they are asking how quickly and effectively it can be embedded into products, processes, decisions and customer experiences. Throughout my career, I have witnessed several technology transitions reshape our industry, from distributed computing and the internet to cloud and digital transformation. What makes AI different is its ability to influence not only technology architectures, but also how organisations operate, make decisions and create value. The next competitive advantage will come from how effectively intelligence is integrated into the operating core of the enterprise.

At Persistent, we believe this is where our engineering heritage creates a distinct advantage. Our roots in software and product engineering have shaped our approach to technology innovation for more than three decades. As enterprises seek to operationalise AI, the combination of product engineering excellence, data expertise, domain knowledge and disciplined execution is becoming increasingly important. Our performance in FY26 reflects the strength of this positioning. Revenue reached $1.654 billion, growing 17.4% year-over-year, while Q4 marked our 24 th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. We are also pleased to announce a final dividend of INR 18 per share, bringing the total dividend for the year to INR 40 per share. These results reflect the growing demand for AI-led modernisation, the dedication of our teams and the trust our clients continue to place in Persistent.

Through our work with enterprises around the world, we have learned that successful AI adoption depends on three critical capabilities: a strong technology foundation, deep business context and the ability to embed intelligence into workflows where decisions and outcomes are created. We describe this through our 3C Framework — Core, Context and Coordination. Together, these capabilities help enterprises move beyond pilots and translate AI investments into measurable business value. This represents a significant opportunity for Persistent. Organisations increasingly need partners that can combine AI capabilities with engineering rigour and accountable execution. Our heritage in product engineering, combined with deep expertise in enterprise modernisation, positions us uniquely to help clients operationalise intelligence across their technology landscape, data estate and business operations. Our AI-led, platform-driven services strategy continues to strengthen this differentiation.

By combining software engineering, cloud, data, platforms and AI, we help clients modernise core systems, accelerate innovation and build more intelligent enterprises. Dear Shareholders, The next phase of enterprise transformation will be defined not by access to AI, but by the ability to operationalise it responsibly, at scale and with measurable business impact. Persistent's performance is ultimately a reflection of its people. As AI reshapes how organisations build, operate and compete, the quality of outcomes increasingly depends on the people responsible for deploying it. As AI becomes embedded in how organisations operate, the most valuable human skills are increasingly shifting from execution to judgement, from information gathering to decision-making and from task completion to problem-solving. AI fluency is becoming foundational, but the ability to apply technology with context, discipline and accountability will determine enterprise success. At Persistent, we believe the advantage of the AI era will not come from technology alone. It will come from the ability to combine engineering expertise, business understanding, judgement and continuous learning to solve increasingly complex challenges. During FY26, we expanded AI learning across every role and career stage.

Structured pathways covered Generative AI, agentic frameworks, Responsible AI and hyperscaler technologies and advanced specialisation tracks developed expertise for increasingly sophisticated engagements. While organisation-wide programmes established AI fluency as a baseline, we also focused on building deeper, applied capabilities by enabling engineers and consultants to use AI with the context, judgement and discipline that complex engagements demand. This shift to applied expertise enabled our teams to leverage AI to improve outcomes and accelerate delivery and value creation. Building the Workforce for the Next Era of Enterprise Execution Persistent University continues to play a central role in this transformation. During the year, employees earned more than 30,000 internal AI certifications, complemented by 24,500+ hyperscaler certifications and 7,000+ external AI and Machine Learning certifications.

Together, these investments continue to expand the depth of AI capability available across our most strategic engagements. Importantly, many of these solutions are developed, tested and refined within Persistent before being deployed at scale. This Customer Zero approach helps accelerate learning, strengthen execution discipline and improve the quality of AI-led solutions delivered to the market. This readiness was demonstrated through Semicolons, our annual global hackathon. More than 1,500 participants across 200+ teams in 25 cities came together to solve 35 real-world challenges contributed by over 25 enterprises. Under the theme, Re(AI)magining the World , teams produced more than 200 working prototypes in a matter of days, demonstrating the speed, creativity and engineering depth that increasingly define AI execution at scale. Building AI capability at scale is becoming increasingly difficult, making talent depth an important source of differentiation.

Organisations that can apply intelligence with business understanding and discipline will be best positioned to create lasting value. Persistent continues to invest in building these strengths. These investments help improve the speed, quality and consistency with which we deliver AI-led outcomes while strengthening a long-term source of competitive differentiation for the company. At Persistent, ESG is not a parallel agenda but a core enabler of long-term resilience, responsible growth and stakeholder trust. As technology reshapes industries and societies, we believe enterprises that combine innovation with accountability and growth with stewardship will define responsible leadership in the AI era, resulting in strengthened operational resilience, responsible decision-making and enduring trust with clients, partners, investors and communities. As a UN Global Compact participant, with Net Zero 2050 targets approved by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), we remain aligned with globally recognised frameworks and climate science. During FY26, we translated ESG commitments into measurable progress. We achieved a 62.90% reduction in market- based emissions and a 20.20% reduction in location-based emissions across Scope 1, 2 and 3 (from the FY24 baseline), while sustaining carbon neutrality for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for the third year in a row.

Global renewable energy adoption rose from 56.83% to 68.22%, with India-owned locations reaching 96.54%.
